page: Amazon Web Services c8in.metal-96xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server configured for compute-intensive and network-heavy applications. Built on an x86_64 architecture powered by Intel processors running at 3.9 GHz, it provides 192 dedicated physical cores supporting 384 vCPUs via two threads per core. System memory totals 768.0 GB of RAM, establishing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

This server platform integrates 600 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, accommodating sustained, high-throughput inter-node traffic. The c8in.metal-96xl instance features zero discrete GPUs and includes no local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent storage and operational disks must be provisioned over network-attached EBS volumes. The absence of local block devices is an operational tradeoff requiring dependency on network storage backends.

With bare-metal execution and dedicated core allocations, the host eliminates virtualization hypervisor overhead. Given its large vCPU count and high networking capability, this server fits distributed compute clusters, large-scale continuous integration or compilation systems, network-bound simulation engines, and parallel batch-processing workloads requiring high processor density.
